purpose: Ustekinumab is used to treat certain immune system conditions including moderate to severe plaque psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, Crohn's disease, and ulcerative colitis. It helps reduce inflammation and relieve symptoms like skin plaques, joint pain, and digestive problems. Your doctor prescribed it because your immune system is overreacting and causing these issues.
how_it_works: Your immune system normally fights infections, but with these conditions it mistakenly attacks your own body and causes inflammation. Ustekinumab works by blocking two specific proteins in your body called IL-12 and IL-23, which are responsible for triggering that overactive response. By blocking these proteins, the medication calms down your immune system and reduces swelling, pain, and other symptoms.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include stuffy or runny nose, sore throat, headache, tiredness, and reactions at the injection site such as redness or soreness. Some people also experience back pain, dizziness, itching, or a mild rash. Most of these are mild and tend to go away on their own.
warnings: Because this medication lowers part of your immune response, you are more likely to get infections, so tell your doctor right away if you develop a fever, chills, or signs of infection. You should not receive live vaccines while on this medication. Tell your doctor if you have ever had tuberculosis or any serious infections. Rare but serious side effects include serious infections, a rare serious brain condition called PML, and a small increased risk of certain cancers. Always let all your healthcare providers know you are taking this medication.
typical_dosing: For psoriasis, the first dose is usually given as an injection under the skin, followed by another dose 4 weeks later, and then every 12 weeks after that. For Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, the very first dose is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion in a clinic, followed by injections under the skin every 8 weeks. Your doctor will decide the exact dose and schedule that is right for you based on your condition and body weight.
